patch.value: pm-graph export --format json emits TOON; neighbors/query reject positional args at contract layer

Two confirmed-live bugs in pm-graph v2026.7.14:

G2 (LOW): 'pm pm-graph export --format json' is accepted but emits TOON ('ok: true ...'), not JSON. Only --json yields JSON. The export command handler ignores --format entirely and always returns {ok, graph} (rendered as TOON by default). Fix: honor --format in the export handler so --format json produces valid JSON on stdout.

G1 (MED): 'pm pm-graph neighbors <node-id>' and 'pm pm-graph query "<cypher>"' reject their documented positional arg at the contract layer ('Too many arguments for extension command'). Root cause: these handlers throw plain Error (no exitCode), which pm's runCommandHandler swallows (handled=false), causing a fall-through to runRequiredExtensionCommand->validateDynamicExtensionCommandArgs; since the command definitions declare no arguments, maxCount=0 and the positional triggers 'Too many arguments'. Sibling commands path/impact work because they throw CommandError (numeric exitCode), which runCommandHandler rethrows and propagates cleanly. Fix: declare the positional arguments on neighbors/query AND throw CommandError so errors propagate cleanly to the clear 'Neo4j not configured' message instead of a contract/usage rejection.

- pm pm-graph export --format json writes valid JSON to stdout (JSON.parse(stdout) succeeds).
- pm pm-graph export (no --format) unchanged (TOON summary), and --json unchanged (JSON of {ok, graph}).
- pm pm-graph neighbors <node-id> accepts the positional and reaches the 'Neo4j not configured' error (not 'Too many arguments').
- pm pm-graph query "<cypher>" accepts the positional and reaches the 'Neo4j not configured' error (not 'Too many arguments').
- pm pm-graph path/impact/cycles/topo-sort/analyze behavior unchanged.
- npm run build && npm test pass.

value.text:
Fixed on branch fix/pm-graph-export-format-json-neighbors-query-args.

G2 (export --format json): The export handler now parses --format; when given, it renders the graph via renderExport and returns the raw payload wrapped in a __pmGraphRawOutput marker. A registered output_format service override (chained, scoped to pm-graph export) unwraps the marker so the host writes the raw string to stdout. --format json now emits a valid JSON Graph document (JSON.parse(stdout) succeeds); default (no --format) and --json are unchanged. Bonus: cypher|mermaid|dot|graphml|plantuml also work via the same path.

G1 (neighbors/query positional rejection): Root cause was NOT a missing arguments declaration per se — path/impact work because they throw CommandError (numeric exitCode), which pm's runCommandHandler rethrows so it propagates cleanly; neighbors/query threw plain Error (no exitCode), which runCommandHandler swallows (handled=false), falling through to runRequiredExtensionCommand->validateDynamicExtensionCommandArgs; since no arguments were declared, maxCount=0 and the positional triggered 'Too many arguments'. Fix: declare the positional arguments on neighbors (node-id) and query (cypher-query, variadic to preserve the multi-token join behaviour) AND throw CommandError so errors propagate cleanly to the clear 'Neo4j not configured' message.

Verified in a throwaway pm workspace: neighbors <id> and query "<cypher>" now reach 'Neo4j is not configured' (exit 1) instead of 'Too many arguments'; missing args now surface as 'Missing required argument' from the contract layer; path/impact/cycles/topo-sort/analyze/critical-path unchanged. 66 tests pass (11 new integration tests covering the contract layer).
